_comment: The known-red proof for every session hook (Stop / UserPromptSubmit), the hook-side sibling of guardrails/gate-red-proofs.json (which covers pre-push gates only and reaches zero hooks). A hook nobody can make fire is a check that watches nothing, the same disease gate-red-proofs.json exists to catch on the push side. guardrails/check-hooks-can-fire.py reads this file: each `proofs` entry names a fixture directory under guardrails/hook-red-fixtures/ that MUST make the hook print a live decision when the hook is run against it for real (no test mocks the hook's own logic — the runner executes the actual script). A `cannot_red` entry names a hook whose own stdout can never carry a verdict by design, with the one-sentence reason, the same shape gate-red-proofs.json's cannot_red carries for a gate that can never fail. A hook classified nowhere, or found under hooks/ or ~/.claude/hooks/ but absent from both maps, is the finding.

scissors-scan.py.note: fires on the English contrast frame 'X, not Y' in the assistant reply

hedge-scan.py.note: fires on the offering-hedge frame 'just say the word'

answer-first-scan.py.note: fires on a reply over the length threshold whose opening paragraph carries no short lead

affirmation-scan.py.note: fires on validating the user ('you're absolutely right', 'great catch')
affirmation-scan.py.source_fallback: no repo copy exists under hooks/ as of this writing; proven against the installed copy at ~/.claude/hooks/affirmation-scan.py — see the census in the movement report

lean-orchestrator-scan.py.note: fires on cumulative inline Read/dump content over the threshold with zero Agent/Task dispatches; OFF by default (opt-in net, guardrails/judge-hooks.json library entry) but still owed a red proof of its own logic

register-judge-report.sh.note: reads a pre-seeded verdict file under $HOME/.claude/hooks/.judge/<session>.json and prints its reason; the runner isolates $HOME to a temp dir per run so no real verdict state is touched

code-anchor-scan.py.note: fires on a queue row number left standing in prose with no plain-word naming of the wish (the 2026-07-27 live failure, verbatim)

cannot_red.register-judge-collect.sh: Hands the turn's text to a background model call (register-judge.py, backgrounded with nohup) and returns immediately with exit 0 and empty stdout by design — the verdict lands asynchronously in a file for register-judge-report.sh to read and print on the human's next turn, so this half's own stdout can never carry a block decision for a fixture to catch; its sibling register-judge-report.sh is proven above instead.
